page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 8 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB per core, and a bundled local SSD storage capacity of 1919 GB. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most compute and memory operations. The server achieves average ratings in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, Passmark CPU and memory scores, and Redis SET operations. However, single-core CPU performance under stress-ng and single-threaded gzip compression are weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Large-model LLM inference is poor, with the 7B model achieving 10.59 tokens per second for prompt processing and 6.28 tokens per second for text generation.

The inclusion of 1919 GB of local SSD storage alongside a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides high resource density for storage-heavy workloads without requiring external block storage. This hardware profile is suited for database operations, static web serving, and memory-intensive tasks that require local scratch space, though it is less efficient for compute-heavy or single-threaded processing tasks due to its lower single-core performance.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.2xlarge is an x86_64 server featuring an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, 64.0 GB of RAM, and 1919 GB of local SSD storage. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, this instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Benchmark results place its multi-core CPU, memory bandwidth, and database operations in the average tier, while single-core performance and single-threaded compression tasks register as weak. Large-model LLM inference performance is poor, making it unsuitable for complex AI workloads. The high local storage capacity and 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio make this server configuration appropriate for database hosting, static web serving, and data-intensive applications requiring significant local storage, offering a balanced resource density for storage-centric workloads.
